consensus_findings.description: test_design_rehydration_matches_canonical_order reads the ephemeral change artifact openspec/changes/write-durable-state-artifacts-guide/design.md, but the suite is registered in the default CI collection (skills/pyproject.toml:129 lists "tests/state-artifacts"). Archival moves changes to openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<change-id>/ (confirmed by the existing entries such as openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-03-route-supervise-gates-through-the-approval-gate-service), so the first cleanup-feature run turns this into a permanent FileNotFoundError on every subsequent CI run of the default suite. This directly contradicts the plan's own selling point at proposal.md:31, 'references remain stable after change archival', and violates the convention the repository already documented at skills/tests/context-engineering/test_promoted_semantic_context_contracts.py:104-107: 'If $id pointed at openspec/changes/<id>/... the reference would resolve into a directory that archival moves — the exact drift the promoted location prevents.' The assertion is also redundant: test_guide_pins_rehydration_order_and_conflict_rules (lines 40-57) already pins the identical eight numbered markers against the durable guide.

The exact eight-stage rehydration sequence (1. Bootstrap locator, 2. Roadmap definition, 3. Roadmap execution state, 4. Change execution state, 5. Learning context, 6. Phase history, 7. Handoff context, 8. Rebuild projections) is consistently specified across design.md, spec.md, docs/guides/state-artifacts.md, and skills/supervise/SKILL.md, and verified by test_state_artifacts_guide.py.

The spec scenario 'Runtime skill mirrors are installed' (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:54-57) has no gate that can fail when installation did not happen. test_changed_skill_mirrors_are_byte_identical calls pytest.skip when either mirror path is absent, and .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/ are gitignored (.gitignore:280-281). A fresh git worktree and a fresh CI checkout therefore both lack the mirrors, so all six parametrized cases skip and the package verification command at work-packages.yaml:110 reports green whether or not task 3.1 ran. The test only detects staleness on machines that already installed the mirrors; it never detects non-installation. Design risk mitigation at design.md:57 acknowledges the CI skip but treats byte comparison as a 'pre-push local gate' without any mechanism that proves the local gate ran.

The 'No-contract context impact is rationalized' verification step invokes validate_context_impact.py with --changed-file pointing at exactly one path (the contracts README). Two consequences follow from the validator's own logic. First, infer_surfaces (skills/validate-packages/scripts/context_impact.py:285-313) only derives surfaces from the files it is given, so with one README the implied set is exactly {apis}; the package's three declared surfaces (documentation, decisions, semantic_code) are never exercised, and a newly implied surface from any other file in the diff cannot be detected. The step is therefore near-tautological as a drift gate. Second, spurious_rationale is a failing status (validate_context_impact.py FAILING_STATUSES) and spurious is computed as set(rationale) - set(implied), so the same package exits 1 under any invocation where the README is not in the changed set, including a re-run scoped to a later base after the README is committed. The repository convention is --base main, used both by skills/validate-packages/SKILL.md:37 and by the archived reference package at openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-26-add-work-package-context-impact-declarations/work-packages.yaml:214.

The six workflow skill documents explicitly use code-quoted repository-relative path references (`docs/guides/state-artifacts.md`) rather than relative markdown links, preserving link validity regardless of runtime mirror nesting depth under `.agents/skills/` or `.claude/skills/`.

The exact set of six workflow skills (autopilot, autopilot-roadmap, session-log, supervise, implement-feature, validate-feature) is consistently maintained across proposal.md, design.md, spec.md, work-packages.yaml, and test_state_artifacts_guide.py.

First-run checkpoint absence for a never-started roadmap is explicitly distinguished from missing state after claimed progress (which is correctly classified as a fail-loud inconsistency/degradation) across design.md, spec.md, docs/guides/state-artifacts.md, and skills/supervise/SKILL.md.

openspec/changes/write-durable-state-artifacts-guide/contracts/README.md correctly declares that no runtime or OpenAPI contract changes, satisfying work-packages.yaml schema requirements for contracts.openapi while providing validated context-impact rationale.

Install mirror verification for .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/ is properly specified in spec.md, implemented in test_state_artifacts_guide.py (test_changed_skill_mirrors_are_byte_identical), and validated in work-packages.yaml via `bash skills/install.sh --check`.

Stage 5 of the rehydration sequence leaves the bounded recent learning window runtime-configurable without hardcoding rigid integer limits, aligning design.md, spec.md, state-artifacts.md, and supervise/SKILL.md.

The plan enforces documentation-only scope discipline using a single sequential work package (wp-state-artifacts-docs) with strict file write_allow lists and key locks, avoiding file overlap and concurrent write conflicts.

The decision to leave the learning window unpinned is correct, but the chosen wording is not accurate and the delivered guide does not match the task. spec.md:21 makes it normative that the learning-context stage 'SHALL use the runtime-configured bounded recent-learning window', and tasks.md:35 lists 'the runtime-configured bounded recent-learning window' as required guide content. The delivered guide says only 'the bounded recent learning window' (docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:25), dropping the qualifier and never naming an owner. The actual referent is RECENCY_WINDOW = 3 at skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/learning.py:27, consumed as the default of recency_window at line 137 and at skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/context.py:55. A repository-wide search finds no non-default caller outside skills/tests/roadmap-runtime/test_learning.py, and no environment variable, CLI flag, or roadmap.yaml field feeds it. So there is no runtime configuration surface, and a reader following the spec will look for one that does not exist. Nothing in the focused suite tests this clause either.

The portability decision recorded at docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md:12 — installed skill payloads cannot use relative Markdown links that escape the skill directory, so skills carry the bare backticked repository path — is guarded by exactly one gate, and the plan never says which. test_canonical_skill_links_to_state_artifacts_guide asserts only that the substring 'docs/guides/state-artifacts.md' appears, which an escaping link such as ../../docs/guides/state-artifacts.md also satisfies. The real enforcement is _local_markdown_link_errors in skills/shared/validate_install_manifest.py:80-106 ('Markdown link escapes installed payload'), reachable only via bash skills/install.sh --check. design.md:57 cites install.sh --check for payload portability in the mirror-drift risk but never connects it to the reference-form decision, so removing that line from the tasks.md:67 validation matrix would silently drop the only guard.

Positive observation. The distinction between a repository-relative reference and a clickable link is applied correctly and deliberately. All six skill sources carry the bare backticked path (identical sentence at skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:17, skills/autopilot-roadmap/SKILL.md:16, skills/session-log/SKILL.md:15, skills/supervise/SKILL.md:17, skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md:22, skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md:22), because those files are copied into .agents/skills/<name>/ and .claude/skills/<name>/ where a relative link out of the skill directory cannot resolve. The documentation index uses a real clickable link, [Durable State Artifacts](state-artifacts.md) at docs/guides/documentation.md:6, which resolves correctly because both files sit in docs/guides/. The rationale is captured at docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md:12 and traced to its phase record at openspec/changes/write-durable-state-artifacts-guide/session-log.md:11.

Positive observation on scope discipline. The six in-scope skills are the correct set. The only other skill that restates loop-state authority is coordination-bridge, whose Work-Queue Truth / Projection Contract section repeats that loop-state.json is authoritative and the queue is a derived projection. That restatement is legitimately owned by a sibling canonical guide: coordination-bridge defers to docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md at line 81, and the state-artifacts guide defers the queue boundary to the same document at docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:15, so the two guides partition rather than duplicate. Its narrower authority list (phase, iteration, package status) is a subset of the guide's row and does not contradict it. The remaining skills that name checkpoint.json — plan-roadmap:87, refine-roadmap:88 and :128, archive-roadmap:13 and :117 — reference it only structurally as a directory entry or as protected execution state, not as ownership semantics. The exclusion was adjudicated on the record in plan-findings.md under the round 1 disposition.

Positive observation on factual accuracy. Every authority and writer claim in the inventory checks out against the runtime. Loop state: the fields named (phase, iteration, package status, gates, transition history) map to current_phase, iteration, packages_status, the gate_decisions/gate_verdict/goal_gate additions in schema version 5, and the append-only outcome log, all in the LoopState dataclass at skills/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py:77-107; the named writer save_state exists at line 155 and runner.py apply-outcome is the cross-process path. Phase records and handoffs: PhaseRecord.write_both exists at skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:355. The local handoff fallback path shape <phase>-<N>.json matches the live artifacts in this change's own handoffs directory (implementation-1.json, plan-fix-1.json). The supervisor mirror and cycle ledger paths match those used by skills/supervise/SKILL.md:139 and :147. Learning entries and their learning-log.md index match skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/learning.py.
The revised proposal, design, delta spec, and tasks consistently make all eight named rehydration stages normative, including projection rebuild after authoritative/advisory reconciliation.
The plan now consistently requires a repository-relative guide reference in exactly the six named workflow skill sources and no longer overstates that requirement as a clickable Markdown link.

The work package explicitly covers strict OpenSpec validation, package validation, the rationalized no-contract context-impact case, install-payload portability, focused state-artifact tests, and diff checks.
The bounded recent-learning window remains runtime-configurable, avoiding a new normative dependency on the current default while preserving deterministic ordering and boundedness.

Nit: Design Rehydration Algorithm step 2 makes the cycle ledger part of the shared eight-stage contract, but the canonical guide omits it while supervise keeps it as local procedure. Evidence: design.md:40 load and validate each named roadmap.yaml plus the cycle ledger; docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:22 only validates roadmap.yaml; skills/supervise/SKILL.md:147 validates roadmap.yaml plus openspec/supervise/cycle-ledger.json; specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:21 names the stage roadmap definition without mentioning the ledger. plan-findings.md already treats cycle-ledger.json as supervise-local operational state outside the five-class authority ladder. Consequence: readers of the guide and design disagree about whether cycle-ledger verification is required for every fresh-session rehydration.

Optional: Residual link wording remains on non-normative surfaces after the portable-reference fix, which can re-blur the repository-relative reference versus clickable Markdown link distinction. Evidence: normative specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:46-51 requires a repository-relative reference and SHALL reference; skills use bare docs/guides/state-artifacts.md; but design.md:50 still says skill links, design.md:54-55 Over-linking / require links, design.md:61 inventory, links, work-packages.yaml:34 replace duplicated skill semantics with links, and docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:44 They link here. The installer rejects escaping relative Markdown links from skill payloads, so clickable-link wording remains a regression hazard even when the SHALL clause is correct.

The exact eight-stage rehydration sequence is consistent across the normative plan surfaces and the drift suite: bootstrap locator, roadmap definition, roadmap execution state, change execution state, learning context, phase history, handoff context, and rebuild/projection rebuild. design.md:39-46, specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:21, docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:21-28, skills/supervise/SKILL.md:139-153, and test_state_artifacts_guide.py ordered markers all name the same stages in the same order, with D3 declaring those stages normative.

First-run checkpoint absence is correctly separated from missing canonical state after claimed progress. specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:31-42 adds Never-started roadmap has no checkpoint versus Canonical state is missing; design.md:23 and design.md:41 require fail-loud handling only when progress is claimed; docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:30-33 states first-run absence is not corruption and claimed prior progress without the artifact is inconsistency.

The no-contract README and package context-impact rationale are coherent for a documentation-only change. contracts/README.md declares no OpenAPI/database/event/generated-type contract; work-packages.yaml points contracts.openapi at that README with an explicit comment; context_impact.rationale.apis explains the schema-required stub and records supervisor approval; validate_context_impact.py against that changed file returns VALID.

On the plan surfaces, the bounded recent-learning window is correctly left runtime-configurable rather than frozen to a numeric default: specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:21 and design.md:43 require a runtime-configured window inside the fixed learning-context stage, matching documentation-only scope (no runtime schema change).
